ev.q: Age-adjusted death rates for deaths with diabetes declined for white and black persons aged ≥65 years from 2005 to 2007
In 2007, the rate was higher for black men and women than for white men and women.
Rates are age-adjusted per 100,000 U.S. standard population aged ≥65 years.
In 2007, diabetes was a contributing cause of death 2.4 times as often as it was the underlying cause
In 2007, the rate was higher for black men and women than for white men and women.
Rates are age-adjusted per 100,000 U.S. standard population aged ≥65 years.
Sources: CDC. National Vital Statistics System.
